title: MySQL Cheatsheet
subtitle: The one-page guide to MySQL: usage, examples, links, snippets, and more.
description: The one-page guide to MySQL: usage, examples, links, snippets, and more.

items.description: Pattern matching (% for any chars, _ for one char)
items.example: SELECT * FROM users WHERE name LIKE 'A%_';

items.description: Filter by regular expression
items.example: SELECT * FROM users WHERE name REGEXP '^A';

items.description: Match against a list of values
items.example: SELECT * FROM users WHERE status IN ('active', 'pending');

items.description: Match values within a range inclusive
items.example: SELECT * FROM users WHERE age BETWEEN 18 AND 30;

items.description: Sort by multiple columns in different directions
items.example: SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY age DESC, name ASC;

items.description: Skip rows and limit results (pagination)
Alias a column or table
items.example: SELECT first_name AS fname FROM users u;

items.description: Rows that have matching values in both tables
items.example: SELECT * FROM a INNER JOIN b ON a.id = b.a_id;

items.description: All rows from right table, matched rows from left
items.example: SELECT * FROM a RIGHT JOIN b ON a.id = b.a_id;

items.description: Cartesian product of both tables
items.example: SELECT * FROM a CROSS JOIN b;

items.description: Join tables sharing the exact same column name
items.example: SELECT * FROM a JOIN b USING (user_id);

items.description: Join a table to itself using aliases
items.example: SELECT a.name, b.name FROM emp a JOIN emp b ON a.mgr_id = b.id;

Insert rows derived from a SELECT query

items.description: Insert rows, ignoring duplicate key errors
Upsert: update row if unique key exists
items.example: INSERT INTO views (url, count) VALUES ('/home', 1) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE count = count + 1;

items.description: Delete using a JOIN condition
items.example: DELETE u FROM users u JOIN logs l ON u.id = l.user_id;

items.description: Limit the number of deleted rows
items.example: DELETE FROM logs WHERE level = 'DEBUG' LIMIT 100;

items.description: Update using a JOIN condition
items.example: UPDATE users u JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id SET u.has_orders = 1;

items.description: Limit the number of updated rows
items.example: UPDATE queue SET status = 'processing' WHERE status = 'pending' LIMIT 10;

Variants for TEXT&BLOB: `TINY` (max=255), `MEDIUM` (max=~16000), and `LONG` (max=4Go). Ex: `VARCHAR(32)`, `TINYTEXT`, `LONGBLOB`, `MEDIUMTEXT`

items.description: Count non-null rows (or all with *)
Sum of column values
Average of column values
Minimum and maximum values
Concatenate column values from a group into a string
items.example: SELECT role, GROUP_CONCAT(name) FROM users GROUP BY role;

items.description: Add summary rows for aggregated totals
items.example: SELECT role, COUNT(*) FROM users GROUP BY role WITH ROLLUP;

items.description: Filter based on a list from a subquery
items.example: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN (SELECT user_id FROM orders);

items.description: Filter based on subquery returning any rows
items.example: SELECT * FROM users u WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = u.id);

items.description: Use a subquery as a derived table in FROM clause
items.example: SELECT temp.id FROM (SELECT id FROM users) AS temp;

items.description: Common Table Expression (CTE) for readable subqueries
items.example: WITH active AS (SELECT * FROM users WHERE status='active') SELECT * FROM active;

items.description: Recursive CTE for hierarchical data
items.example: WITH RECURSIVE cnt(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1 FROM cnt WHERE n<5) SELECT * FROM cnt;

items.description: Assign sequential integer to each row in partition
items.example: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary) FROM emp;

items.description: Rank rows, with gaps for ties
items.example: SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) FROM scores;

items.description: Rank rows, without gaps for ties
items.example: SELECT DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) FROM scores;

items.description: Access value from a previous row

items.description: Access value from a subsequent row
items.example: SELECT LEAD(price) OVER (ORDER BY date) FROM sales;

items.description: Calculate running total or partition sum
items.example: SELECT SUM(sales) OVER (PARTITION BY store_id) FROM orders;

items.description: Combine results from queries, removing duplicates

items.description: Combine results from queries, keeping duplicates
